text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED to #eng-runtime — GPU ECC error spike on pool-gd-13. alert_id=ECC_SPIKE_47, severity=sev2, started=1790001220

alyssa: saw the page. where is pool-gd-13 physically?

jordan: asia-east1 (aka cluster-rd-asia). restarting one of the pods now, will report.

nate: quick telemetry — VRAM pressure spiking on node gd-13-04, temps ~86C, ECC errs count jumped to 14 in 2m. :thermometer:

samir: are we seeing customer errors? any 5xxs?

alyssa: yes, a few customer requests for streaming failed with `socket reset` and gen latency increased ~2-3x for requests routed to that node. routing fallback did kick in for some but not all.

incident-bot: background: alert fires when ECC_ERR_COUNT > 5 in 60s OR ECC_RATE > 0.08. noise_suppression=false for that rule.

jordan: evicting pods from gd-13-04 and cordoning node. running: `kubectl drain gd-13-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ops-bot: drain started at 1790001305 — 8 pods to migrate. ETA ~45s per pod depending on warm cache.

nate: adding note: one OOM killer event at 1790001280 on ms-infer-3. probably memory blow due to degraded kernel behavior during ECC spikes.

samir: any thermal fan/sensor alerts from host?

eva: host shows fan pwm at 100%, temp trending up after a recent microcode update (we pushed at 1790000500).

alyssa: could be microcode + workload steering. let's not jump to firmware rollback yet. keep node cordoned, pods on other nodes for now.

jordan: node gd-13-04 now cordoned and drained. pods backfilled to gd-12-* and gd-14-*. routing policy routed ~60% of requests off the node.

incident-bot: mitigation result: customer error rate reduced to baseline after 3 mins. some p99 latency residuals for long sequences.

samir: propose immediate mitigations: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) mark as restricted for high-memory batches, 3) add short-term ECC aggregation suppression on alert rule to avoid paging noise while we investigate. thoughts?

nate: agree. suppression window 10m while we gather diagnostics. but log raw events to S3 for postmortem.

alyssa: owner for diagnostics = jordan. owner for alert tuning = samir. owner for dashboard + perf check = eva.

jordan: dumping ECC logs now. snippet:
```
# nvme_gpu_ecc_dump
timestamp: 1790001322
device: gd-13-04
ecc_events: [3,2,4,5]
cuda_jobs: [job-987, job-654]
```

nate: adding note: VRAM used peaked at 98% on the offending pod. suggests a working set blow-up plus kernel/driver retries causing memory retention.

samir: for the alert tuning: current rule fires on any >=1 ECC err in 60s. that's too noisy for these clusters — propose change: alert when ECC_ERR_COUNT >= 5 over 5m AND ECC_RATE > 0.05 AND VRAM_UTIL > 90% OR THERMAL > 85C. That should reduce false positives.

eva: +1. also add a new Grafana panel for per-node combined view: ECC events, VRAM, temp, fan pwm, OOMs in one row so oncall can triage quicker. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/gpu-health (placeholder)

alyssa: agree but be careful: we still want a hard alarm for catastrophic single-event ECC that indicates hardware failure. maybe keep a suppressed sev3/quiet channel for single events and only escalate to sev2 when the aggregated rule triggers.

samir: implemented draft rule in staging alerts repo. snippet:
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_AVG_SPIKE
  expr: increase(gpu_ecc_events_total[5m]) >= 5 and avg_over_time(gpu_vram_util[5m]) > 0.90
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: >-
      Check node temps, fan pwm, recent microcode/driver changes. If ECC errors continue after cordon, escalate to hardware subsystem.
```

nate: also suggest a temporary mute on the noisy `ECC_SPIKE_47` rule in alertmanager for 10m. I'll do that now.

ops-bot: alertmanager mute applied by nate for 10m at 1790001380 — rule=ECC_SPIKE_47.

alyssa: customers impacted list? who saw errors?

jordan: customer abc-corp saw ~0.8% requests fail during the 6m window; latency tail for streaming rose from 1.2s to 3.8s on requests routed to gd-13-04. logged ids: [req-44321, req-44322, req-44350]. I triggered support ticket #SUP-3321 to inform account team.

samir: post-incident actions (P0):
- Short-term: keep node cordoned until HW team validates (owner: jordan, due: 1790001800).
- Mid-term: adjust alert thresholds and add combined dashboard (owner: eva, due: 1790002200).
- Long-term: add adaptive suppression to avoid noisy pages during transient microcode flaps (owner: samir, due: 1790008000).

alyssa: add test plan: simulate ECC noise in staging with `gpu-ecc-sim` and verify alerts don't spam on transients but still escalate on sustained errors. (owner: nate).

nate: will create a canary job in staging and put test results into the incident ticket.

jordan: capturing packet-level kernel logs and uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1790001234/gd-13-04-logs.tar.gz

eva: working on dashboard wireframe now. will post link when ready.

incident-bot: NOTE: microcode update at 1790000500 flagged in host-change-log. Recommend HW team review microcode + driver compatibility for that batch of nodes.

alyssa: ok, summary for handoff: gd-13-04 cordoned/drained; ECC spike likely correlated with recent microcode push; mitigation=drain+route fallback; customer impact limited but visible for abc-corp; tuning plan proposed to reduce alert noise while retaining escalation; owners assigned.

samir: i'll own the alert PR. i'll post the change to `ops/alerts` and request review.

jordan: handing off to HW escalation team now — pinging @hw-oncall via ticket. leaving channel.

alyssa: thanks all. please post any new findings to #eng-runtime and append to ticket SUP-3321.

ops-bot: handoff recorded at 1790001800 — incident transitioned to hardware ops.

alyssa: follow-up action items: create new dashboard, update runbook with microcode checklist, PR for alert change, staging test. we'll review in next weekly ops retro. :white_check_mark:
